PullRequest.Title: agentHost: native Mission Control environments
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Expose VS Code's existing native Agent Host utility process as an opt-in user-local Mission Control environment over Azure Web PubSub. Local sessions continue using local IPC; remote clients use the same native session state and protocol handler. No separate daemon is launched.

The URI prerequisite [#339492](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339492) has merged. This PR now targets `main`, merged locally in `d9b4cd31dd3`.

- Register, heartbeat, withdraw and recover the environment using trusted local credentials, canonical-owner checks and a stable random profile-local compute identity.
- Enforce signed control, sealed identity/MCP authentication, lane/client-ID binding, passive access, relay workspace/resource grants, and host-management/root-configuration restrictions.
- Discover/connect to existing user-local environments with cached-first inventory and background refresh; retain the existing managed-sandbox flow.
- Mirror authoritative AHP actions and selected genuine SDK metadata with bounded spools, durable acknowledgements and signed retained backfill. Native titles and activity update MC's task catalog.
- Support the opt-in path in built desktop products as well as source builds, retaining the existing default-off experimental setting keys.
- Use product display names, ordinary Mission Control class/management names, and a scoped DI-backed native adapter. Node implementation lives under `node/missionControl/`.
- Consume negotiated standard session URIs from the prerequisite without global provider aliases or historical URI/storage rewriting.
- Keep host-wide diagnostic logs off relay ingress, backpressure mirror publication without dropping retained frames, bound unanswered AHP handshakes, and recover transient identity-validation faults without treating refused credentials as compatible.

No separate VS Code issue is linked; this is the user-local environment integration. Environment-management UX alongside SSH/dev tunnels is a separate follow-up.

## Security scope and remaining qualification

Remote owner access includes sessions, tools and granted workspace resources. MC stores mirrored conversation content; credential sealing is not conversation E2EE.

Mandatory handshake binding, per-client/session credential sponsorship, OS containment, response-part ID continuity and full durable AHP restart/history baselines remain accepted deferrals. Unbound sealed tokens remain replayable, active credentials use the existing shared native provider store, and path grants do not claim OS confinement.

See the [security requirements and sources](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/680d699afd12266e3e42d5fb2db6b4723f77178b/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/MISSION_CONTROL_SECURITY_REQUIREMENTS.md), [remaining gaps](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/680d699afd12266e3e42d5fb2db6b4723f77178b/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/MISSION_CONTROL_PRODUCTION_GAPS.md), and [operation/configuration](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/680d699afd12266e3e42d5fb2db6b4723f77178b/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/MISSION_CONTROL.md). The source matrix groups 35 requirements by security topic and distinguishes Copilot Host contracts, protocol specifications, user choices and assistant-proposed adaptations. It was independently reviewed for clarity and pinned-source consistency.

GitHub-authoritative authorization expiry, durable per-session mirror opt-out, enterprise endpoint coherence/disclosure, and independent operator-owned session/repository policy remain identified gaps, not implicitly accepted deferrals.

An older signed macOS arm64 artifact passed registration, crypto loading, native/remote execution and withdrawal. Final-head packaged qualification, Windows/Linux and enterprise deployment, and completed three-hour reliability qualification remain outstanding. No review requirement or release/privacy approval is overridden by this PR.

## How to exercise

1. Sign in to GitHub in a desktop window and leave `chat.agentHost.experimentalMissionControlFakeEndpoint` empty.
2. Enable `chat.agentHost.experimentalMissionControl.enabled`, using the default trusted HTTPS endpoint.
3. Wait for `Mission Control ready; environmentId=...` in the Agent Host log.
4. Create/use a native session normally over local IPC.
5. From a separate matching-owner client, discover the environment, authenticate through the relay and list/open/drive that same session. In another VS Code instance, use **Connect to Mission Control Environment...**.
6. Verify task title/activity, disconnect/reconnect, and owner withdrawal. Offline user-local attachment does not provision replacement compute.

The local test-endpoint setting is only for a trusted loopback HTTP integration-test server; the local GitHub credential is sent there if explicitly configured.

## Validation

Current head: `680d699afd1`; the latest changes are documentation-only. Runtime code is unchanged from the tested implementation at `0622f8dd27e`. Client output was refreshed incrementally after merging `main`. Local validation:

- `npm run typecheck-client` — **passed**.
- `npm run test-node -- --runGlob '**/agentHost/test/node/{missionControl*,protocolServerHandler,copilotSessionLauncher}.test.js'` — **423 passed**.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/browser/webPubSubRelayTransport.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxConnectionCustomization.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxApiService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxAgentHostService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts` — **1,685 passed**, 11 existing pending.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — **passed**.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/agentHostProtocolClient.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/webPubSubRelayTransport.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/protocolServerHandler.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/missionControlAuthentication.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/missionControlHost.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/missionControlProtocolServer.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/missionControlSessionMirror.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxConnectionCustomization.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxApiService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxTelemetry.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxConnectionCustomization.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts` — **passed**.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts` — **passed**.
- `node build/lib/formatter.ts --replace --verify src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts` — **passed**, formatting-only corrections.
- `git diff --cached --check` and normal commit hooks — **passed**.
- Documentation target resolution, all 35 sequential requirement IDs and cross-references — **passed**.

**Current-head CI passed:** [Code OSS](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37381170894) completed all 21 jobs successfully at `680d699afd1`, including compile/hygiene and Linux/macOS/Windows unit, integration, browser, smoke and remote tests. CodeQL, Component Fixtures/Screenshots, Monaco, chat-lib, telemetry, dependency, license and PR-policy checks also passed.

The [previous-head Code OSS run](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37375389714) was interrupted by killed lint/tsec processes, a browser-runner shutdown and a smoke-step deadline after 66 passing tests. The fresh run passed without changing runtime code or weakening any check or timeout.

Real isolated, sync-disabled two-instance runs exercised native remote turns and verified shell output in both host directions. A completed two-hour run recorded 2,470 snapshots, 15 remote turns, 71 verified terminals and eight deliberate same-client reconnects. Original-owner replay covered 92 sessions/184 snapshots, including a 1,546,452-byte chat. Held application subscriptions recovered across deliberate host socket loss in about 28.4 seconds with no subscription errors and subsequent remote work.

Unexpected host socket-close cause remains unconfirmed. A three-hour attempt was reboot-interrupted; its resumed run ended after about 104 minutes when the automation connection closed, with the apps/debugging endpoints still live afterward. Neither attempt completed three-hour qualification. These bounded observations are not fleet-stability or security certification.

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The pending-set gate, shared FIFO, acknowledgement-driven drain, per-action mirror admission, and explicit serialization/backlog tests establish the mechanism and realistic trigger. Actual service RTT and workload prevalence are not measured; the latency relationship follows statically from the code.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Web PubSub publication slots and sequential network acknowledgement waits shared by all lanes and mirror namespaces.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For Q frames ahead of a response and acknowledgement interval R, send latency grows approximately Q×R rather than allowing a bounded batch in flight. Q is the admitted FIFO backlog, not the entire retained history; mirror admission caps it at 128 frames before byte limits, and chunking increases frame count for larger payloads.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Head-of-line blocking of interactive remote responses and reduced aggregate relay throughput during streaming or replay.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Native sessions delivered through the existing local IPC/WebSocket handlers without this service-acknowledgement gate or shared mirror backlog. The existing Web PubSub client transport also writes all message fragments in order while tracking acknowledgements independently.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new native Mission Control publisher shares one outbound FIFO across interactive lane messages and historical/live mirror events, and allows only one publication awaiting a Web PubSub acknowledgement.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added condition `while (this._pending.size === 0 && this._outbound.length > 0)` at line 290 stops after `_pending.add(next.ackId)` and resumes only when acknowledgement handling deletes that ID. Added `_publish()` and `publishMirrorEvent()` both append to this same `_outbound` queue.
Findings.Title: Allow bounded pipelining instead of globally awaiting each publish ack
Findings.Impact: After reconnect/backfill, or while native sessions stream actions, an initialize/file/dispatch response behind Q already-admitted frames cannot even be sent until those Q acknowledgements arrive. With 128 queued small mirror frames this creates roughly 128 sequential service-acknowledgement waits; additional client lanes share the same bottleneck. This delays remote attachment and interaction and limits aggregate streaming throughput to one frame per acknowledgement interval.
Findings.Evidence: MissionControlHost._createMirror forwards each authoritative action to mirror.enqueue, including individual SDK ChatDelta emissions (copilotAgentSession.ts:2574–2604). MissionControlProtocolServer._enqueue uses a single FIFO; _drain adds the acknowledgement before socket.send; _receive at lines 339–364 removes it and drains again. Mirror admission permits 128 queued frames/16 MiB, and the whole FIFO permits 512 frames/64 MiB. The new tests explicitly expect only one of two responses before an acknowledgement, and exercise 600-frame historical backlogs with an initialize reply queued during the backlog. In contrast, webPubSubRelayTransport.ts:473–482 sends every fragment without awaiting prior acknowledgements.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep bounded backpressure and required per-lane ordering, but permit a bounded in-flight publication window with acknowledgement tracking rather than global stop-and-wait; ensure bulk mirror/replay traffic cannot monopolize interactive response delivery.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous pre-dispatch guard, filesystem calls, non-deduplicated root construction, asynchronous underlying read, and shared-process ownership are directly traced. Exact mount latency and frequency of later-root matches are uncertain, so severity is medium; no benchmark duration is assumed.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous filesystem realpath, lstat, and stat operations on the shared Agent Host event loop.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For F file requests, an existing target costs F target canonicalizations plus the sum of roots visited before each match; absent targets add ancestor checks. Cold and warm requests both repeat these calls. Root cardinality is explicit grants plus loaded/resident workspace/content entries, with early exit and the normal 10-session residency target accounted for.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Event-loop stalls and serialized metadata I/O causing slower file browsing and interference with local and remote agent activity on slow filesystems.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The existing native resource handlers used asynchronous file-service operations; there was no relay-specific synchronous realpath/stat authorization loop running ahead of dispatch in the shared Agent Host process.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Relay resource requests now synchronously canonicalize the requested file or its existing ancestors, then synchronously canonicalize each grant visited before a match, before dispatching the existing asynchronous operation.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `relative(realpathSync(root), canonical)` at line 2295 is inside a per-request roots.some loop. The diff also adds target realpathSync/lstatSync/statSync and calls `_requireRelayResourceAccess()` synchronously from _handleRequest before invoking asynchronous handlers.
Findings.Title: Perform relay path canonicalization off the host event loop
Findings.Impact: Browsing a mounted workspace or opening several changed files adds blocking filesystem calls to every relay read/list/resolve. Even a first-root match repeats target and root canonicalization; a later worktree/content-root match additionally visits preceding roots, including duplicate resident-session workspaces. Slow mount metadata operations stall the shared host event loop, delaying local session progress and other remote lanes as well as the file request.
Findings.Evidence: ProtocolServerHandler._handleRequest:2011–2012 invokes the guard synchronously. _isGrantedRelayResource:2265–2305 resolves the target/ancestors synchronously and then realpaths grants until the first match. MissionControlHost._resourceRoots:106–112 rebuilds `[...grantedRoots, ...residentSessionWorkspaces, ...sessionContentRoots]` without deduplicating workspaces. The handler uses the same AgentService/state manager and utility-process event loop as local IPC. AgentService.resourceRead:9613 awaits fileService.readFile. Residency normally targets 10 sessions but exempts subscribed/active/held sessions; this is not a loop over all persisted history.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve symlink/grant enforcement but perform canonicalization/stat checks asynchronously before dispatch, maintaining required action ordering. Deduplicate roots within a check; do not cache canonical paths across filesystem/grant changes without appropriate invalidation.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The first OS lookup per connection unnecessarily awaited full network-diagnostics metadata. On a signed-in native host with cold/expired Copilot endpoint context this crossed IPC/RPC and waited for `/copilot_internal/user` endpoint discovery even though root-state resources already advertised the OS.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Opening an Agent Host scoped file dialog can wait for endpoint-discovery network latency before path formatting completes. The two dialog OS/path lookups coalesce into one diagnostics request per connection; endpoint/login resolution also shares one token-context fetch, not two independent network calls.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new advertised-platform branch reads the already-present root resource metadata and returns immediately, avoiding the diagnostics IPC/RPC and its cold-token endpoint fetch. The existing WeakMap still coalesces and retains the per-connection OS result; unsupported/absent metadata retains the old fallback.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 27 unconditionally awaited connection.getNetworkDiagnosticsInfo(); blame attributes it to the stated commit. Added lines 28–37 read resource platform and return before that await. AgentHostStateManager:355 already publishes collectAgentHostResources() in root metadata. AgentHostConnectionsService:50–51 registers the OS provider, _getOperatingSystem:153 awaits the helper, and SimpleFileDialog:339 awaits resolvePathFormatting, whose lines 1077–1080 request OS/path concurrently. AgentService:10070–10072 awaits provider diagnostics. CopilotAgent:1517–1535 resolves endpoint/login; both use CopilotApiService._getEntryForToken:902 onward, sharing a pending/token-keyed 30-minute context, and _buildClientForToken:1023 onward performs the `/copilot_internal/user` fetch on a miss. No connectivity probes are involved. Thus the removed critical-path network dependency is concrete, though warm token contexts previously avoided HTTP.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ordinary native Agent Host startup with Mission Control disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Native host construction and existing local IPC startup proceed without registration. MissionControlHost constructs its adapter, but mirror creation, SDK metadata observation, registration and sealing initialization require explicit enablement.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One adapter per native host; no per-session Mission Control work while never enabled.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No Mission Control network, SDK-history or crypto initialization jobs are launched on ordinary construction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Neither registration caches nor crypto initialization are populated on the default-off path. The heavy crypto implementation is dynamically loaded only for opt-in/sealing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: registration/mirror attachment are guarded by configure/enablement; construction alone does not invoke them.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Static review; ordinary constructor allocations were not profiled.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence startup regression on the default-off path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable native Mission Control, register the device, and maintain heartbeat/policy metadata
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration crosses management IPC, validates identity/grants, computes session count then reads authoritative remote-control policy, registers, obtains signing keys when needed and connects/joins the relay. These operations gate advertised host readiness, not unrelated local turn dispatch. Periodic check-ins normally run at 60-second cadence.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/missionControlHost.ts: environment configuration/attachment and native management service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Configure or withdraw the native host through the existing local management channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration request per relevant settings/account/workspace update; not one per session or environment row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No native Mission Control configuration operation on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configuration completion gates enablement/readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Canonicalize grants/user-data directory and read/create/migrate the profile's compute-identity file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Canonicalization scales with configured roots per configure; identity-file work is per profile bootstrap/restart, with a retained compute ID afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Native host startup did not persist/canonicalize Mission Control identity/grants.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before registration identity/grants are established.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the session catalog for registration/heartbeat counts, using existing catalog batching and metadata fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One listSessions computation per actual check-in, shared with overlapping same-mode/epoch computations; central catalog work is batched, fallback metadata is limited to four concurrent jobs. Settled counts are not cached indefinitely.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The catalog/listSessions mechanism already existed; Mission Control adds its periodic/registration invocation, not a new per-session SDK RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Count completion precedes the check-in request; registration metadata waits are bounded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ensure the shared Copilot SDK runtime and read its authoritative managed-settings document.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK read per live metadata check-in/policy reconciliation; cold runtime can require shared SDK startup, warm runtime reuses the client. No per-session reads are added here.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: SDK/client/settings facilities existed, but the native Mission Control check-in did not invoke them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before registration/heartbeat metadata is submitted; does not gate local AHP action dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate live owner via GitHub /user, register/check in, obtain WPS credentials/signing keys and connect the relay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Owner validation is configuration/authentication scoped; one register/heartbeat request per effective check-in, one JWKS request on cold/expired five-minute signing-key cache, and one socket connection per bootstrap/recovery. Bootstrap joins control and, when mirroring, ingest-ack groups; client-group joins occur per verified lane.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No native-host registration/heartbeat/socket traffic; existing cloud/other host transports were separate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial operations gate remote readiness; periodic maintenance is background work with bounded HTTP waits.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured roots, stored catalog sessions for count computation, relevant configuration changes, heartbeat cadence and recovery attempts—not environments times sessions times requests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One in-flight check-in per generation; session-count collection precedes policy collection, then the network check-in. Catalog fallbacks are limited to four. Retry/Retry-After logic prevents a rapid check-in burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Compute identity is retained; shared SDK client is reused; catalog calls coalesce in flight but have no settled count cache; JWKS TTL is five minutes. Heartbeat/policy checks remain authoritative. Crypto is initialized lazily.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: metadata callbacks, sequential awaits, timer cadence, generation fencing and boundaries were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog sizes, SDK cold-start duration and service latency are not measured. SDK policy reads have no narrower safe API established here.
Scenarios.Verdict: New opt-in work is bounded and required for registration/authoritative policy; no separate high-confidence regression beyond the reported synchronous per-request filesystem mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover environments, select a native host, seal credentials and attach/reconnect
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Picker displays cached inventory immediately when available and refreshes in the background. Cold inventory is needed to populate choices. Selection revalidates one environment and then obtains broker credentials, establishes WPS/AHP and authenticates. The self-host identity check avoids a redundant loopback connection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch environment inventory, revalidate the selected descriptor and mint/refresh relay credentials.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inventory request for a cold or explicit-refresh invocation, serving every environment row; zero for a valid non-refresh cache lookup. One selected-environment revalidation and selected connection operation; reconnect intentionally refreshes broker credentials once per attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cloud broker operations existed; native environment discovery/selection and user-local reconnect placement are added. The picker does not introduce a network request per row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Warm picker refresh is background; selected-host descriptor and connection credentials gate attachment.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check native self-environment identity and seal authentication credentials through native management.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One self-identity lookup for the selection workflow; one sealing call per credential-sealing request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No native Mission Control self-host/sealing management requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Identity/sealing must complete before the corresponding remote attach; self-selection can avoid attach altogether.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxAgentHostService.ts: native descriptor/sealing and protocol authentication; src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/missionControlAuthentication.ts: resolveMissionControlOwner
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Obtain the selected environment's sealing descriptor and validate the unsealed authentication owner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Descriptor fetch is per sealing request, not per environment/session; owner /user validation is per authentication attempt. Descriptor reads are not independently cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Native sealed-credential authentication and its descriptor/owner calls did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates successful relay authentication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh authoritative root state after identity authentication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Concurrent refreshes share one pending root-refresh operation per transport; later authentication can trigger another refresh. Not one refresh per session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The authenticated-native-relay root-refresh placement is added; normal protocol snapshot transport machinery already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authentication/root availability is bounded by the refresh wait before consumers use the authenticated snapshot.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Environment rows affect local picker processing; network counts scale with picker invocations, selected connections, authentication/sealing requests and reconnect attempts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Inventory is a single collection request, not row fan-out. Connection sequencing awaits descriptor/credentials/authentication; concurrent root refreshes coalesce per transport. Separate deliberate picker invocations can issue separate refreshes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Inventory has account/discovery-generation keying, a 60-second TTL and caches valid empty results. Explicit picker refresh bypasses cached results but cached values can display immediately. Root refreshes coalesce in flight; broker credentials deliberately refresh on reconnect.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inventory cache, cached-first picker, selected-descriptor flow, credential refresh and root single-flight were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Service latency and simultaneous picker use are unmeasured; no large effective per-row boundary multiplicity is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate high-confidence discovery/sealing regression. Attachment responses can suffer the reported host-global outbound acknowledgement/FIFO bottleneck when mirror replay is queued.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stream native/local and remote turns while mirroring authoritative actions, including reconnect/backfill
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Local AHP dispatch synchronously notifies the mirror source but does not await cloud durability. Remote consumers must receive protocol replies/notifications; their publication uses the same FIFO as live/historical mirror traffic. Reconnect reattaches retained publication and can create an admitted backlog before an interactive reply.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clone/serialize each authoritative envelope, build bounded event/chunk frames and serialize outbound protocol/mirror messages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One AHP mirror admission per emitted session envelope, including individual ChatDelta actions; subscribed relay lanes additionally receive protocol notifications. Large messages expand to their actual chunk count. SDK mirror metadata is independent, not every raw SDK token event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Local/native dispatch had existing subscriber transport serialization but no native Mission Control mirror clone/spool/event framing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Envelope admission has synchronous CPU/allocation cost on host dispatch; transport/durable acknowledgement waits are not awaited by local dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish interactive client frames and mirror user events over one WPS socket, tracking service acknowledgements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only one publication in flight globally. Mirror admission is capped at 128 queued frames/16 MiB and the whole FIFO at 512/64 MiB; the actual frames ahead of a reply, not all retained history, determine its sequential acknowledgement waits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Native IPC/WebSocket delivery had no Mission Control service-ack gate/backlog. Existing client-side WPS sends ordered fragments without awaiting each preceding service acknowledgement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: An interactive reply behind Q admitted frames waits approximately Q service-acknowledgement intervals before it can be sent; aggregate stream throughput is one frame per acknowledgement interval.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Concurrent streaming sessions, emitted action frequency, subscribed relay lanes, payload chunk count and admitted replay backlog. Remote notifications and mirrors share one global publication capacity rather than separate per-lane capacity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Local turns are not blocked on network durability. Mirror flush is bounded per scheduler turn, and admission backpressures on queue limits, but all outbound publications use a global single pending service acknowledgement. Adding lanes does not increase throughput.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AHP and SDK spools are independently bounded: per-namespace defaults include 32 MiB/session and 128 MiB total plus frame/session caps; transport acknowledgements free publication capacity, while durable ingest watermarks release retained data. Backfill reuses retained frames; attachment is not a cold-history read for every lane.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: shared FIFO, pending-set gate, per-action mirror call path, chunking, limits and explicit stop-and-wait/backlog tests establish the mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual WPS acknowledgement interval and action rate are not measured. Long replay/streaming workloads are realistic; severity reflects their impact rather than invented latency numbers.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported high-severity head-of-line blocking/throughput regression at missionControlProtocolServer.ts:290. Additional serialization is real but no independent excessive-work regression was established; retention is bounded rather than unbounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reconcile SDK metadata journals, reserve durable sequence ranges and synchronize native titles
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Optional SDK metadata jobs are off the local AHP critical path. Initial/resumed journal reconciliation precedes that session's metadata tail publication; durable acknowledgement/cursor persistence maintains replay state. Metadata uses the same relay publisher already analyzed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stream the native SDK event journal to reconcile initial metadata or locate a persisted cursor and emit its tail.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial reconciliation per observed source session; cursor replay scans the journal for the cursor when history work is required. Reads use 64 KiB chunks and a bounded line size, not full-history materialization per emitted event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing SDK journals existed, but native Mission Control did not perform these replication scans.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates optional metadata replay for that source, not native AHP dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/update environment-specific SDK sequence reservations and durable journal cursors in session databases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Sequence reservations allocate blocks of 1,024 rather than a write per metadata frame. Initial source reads retrieve sequence/cursor state; durable cursor writes coalesce through acknowledgement/drain processing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Session databases existed without these Mission Control reservation/cursor keys and updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reservation precedes optional metadata admission; cursor persistence is asynchronous and not awaited by local AHP dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize the authoritative title to an already-live SDK backing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Attempted for changed/unsynchronized titles; a successful value is cached on the source. No SDK process/session is created solely for this update, and successful synchronization is not repeated per streamed token. Failed/unavailable attempts may be retried by later drains.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No native Mission Control-driven SDK-title synchronization on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background metadata drain only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish filtered SDK metadata and replay events over the shared mirror transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per deduplicated admitted metadata frame/tail event, constrained by independent SDK credits and byte/frame budgets; shares the one global outbound publication slot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No native SDK metadata mirror publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Metadata replay can wait for SDK mirror capacity and WPS publication; not local dispatch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Observed sessions and their journal bytes/tail metadata, not all persisted sessions at ordinary startup. Live queues and deduplication use bounded event/byte/ID counts; SDK state events, not every raw text delta, control persistence work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Global limiter of four metadata jobs plus per-source drain coalescing; replay waits for mirror capacity and supports cancellation. Live queues are bounded per session and globally. This is not unbounded Promise.all across sessions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-source history state avoids repeated initial reconciliation; a 512-ID seen set deduplicates events. Successful title values are cached, negative/unavailable synchronization is not assumed cached. Sequence/cursor state is environment/session keyed and persisted for continuity.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: limiter, per-source state, streaming reader, sequence blocks, cursor drains and live-backing title behavior were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large journal sizes and slow database/SDK durations are unmeasured. Cold journal scans are additional feature work but are bounded/concurrent-limited and off local dispatch.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate high-confidence metadata/history regression. Shared publication serialization is covered by the reported outbound finding; no duplicate claim of per-token RPC/database work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse/read/mutate remote workspace resources and open a terminal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Relay requests synchronously pass grant/symlink validation before reaching asynchronous resource handlers or requested terminal creation. Completion then crosses the relay response queue. Local IPC and SDK progress share the utility-process event loop used by the validation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronously realpath target/ancestors and visited grants; stat/lstat missing-path ancestors or terminal cwd.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For F existing file requests: F target canonicalizations plus the sum of grant entries visited before a match. Missing targets add ancestor checks; copy/move validate two fields; terminal cwd adds an existence/type stat. Grants include explicit roots plus resident/loaded session workspaces and read-only content directories. Duplicated workspaces are not grouped; first match short-circuits. Normal residency target is 10, with subscribed/active/held exemptions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No relay-specific synchronous authorization loop ahead of the existing asynchronous native resource operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the shared host event loop before async dispatch, affecting local and other remote work during slow filesystem calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform requested file read/list/resolve/write/copy operations through existing file services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One corresponding resource operation per UI request after authorization; original resource grouping and per-resource write sequencing remain. The guard adds metadata calls, not a duplicate full file read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same native resource handlers already performed these async operations; the new relay routes to them after the added synchronous checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Necessary for the requested file result; ordinarily asynchronous.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read referenced edit content from the owning session's database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per actual session-db content request, using existing session database ownership; non-file authorization does not execute the filesystem-root loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing session-db resource handling; the diff adds relay access validation and reachability, not extra database reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Necessary for the requested edit preview.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read a requested Git blob with the existing Git operation, or create the terminal explicitly requested by the client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per actual blob/terminal request; no subprocess per grant or per session-summary entry is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing native Git-content and terminal handlers; relay access checks/routing are new, their underlying operations are not duplicated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for requested Git content/terminal after authorization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transmit remote resource RPCs and serialize/publish their results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per resource request/result, expanded by actual chunk count for large payloads. Responses share the host-global publication slot with mirrors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Local native requests used IPC/other existing transports without this Mission Control response path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remote file completion requires delivery; publication may wait behind replay frames.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Remote file-operation frequency, requested path depth/absence, explicit grant count and resident workspace/content entries visited before matching. Mounted workspace metadata latency is a realistic amplifier; total persisted session history is not the grant-loop cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Authorization is synchronously serialized on the event loop even when requests arrive from multiple lanes. Underlying filesystem handlers are async and retain their existing queues; outbound results additionally encounter global stop-and-wait.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Target and visited-root canonicalization repeat on both cold and warm requests; no application-level grouping/cache was found. OS filesystem caches may reduce duration but do not make synchronous calls non-blocking. Non-file Git/session-db previews use separate authorization and avoid this loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: synchronous call placement, filesystem operations, root composition, early exit/residency constraints and shared host ownership were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Slow-mount prevalence and individual metadata-call durations are unknown; medium severity reflects that uncertainty without suppressing the concrete blocking mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported medium-severity synchronous filesystem regression at protocolServerHandler.ts:2295. Existing requested file/Git/database/terminal work is not independently reported; relay response blocking shares the publisher root cause.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve host-specific path formatting for an Agent Host file dialog
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SimpleFileDialog awaits resolvePathFormatting. Its OS/path requests coalesce through the per-connection OS WeakMap; the old helper required diagnostics before formatting could proceed. The new helper reads the already-advertised platform when valid.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch full host network-diagnostics metadata just to obtain OS when advertised-platform resolution is unavailable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before: one request per cold connection, including coalesced simultaneous dialog OS/path queries; subsequent successes reuse the OS result. After: zero when the advertised platform is valid; otherwise same fallback and failure eviction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unconditionally invoked diagnostics on the first lookup even when root resources already supplied platform.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously on first scoped-dialog path-formatting critical path; removed for valid platform metadata.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover Copilot token context/endpoints via /copilot_internal/user on a cold/expired signed-in token context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Endpoint and account resolutions share one token-keyed pending/context fetch, not two requests. Warm 30-minute context avoids HTTP; cold/refresh-required context can issue one request. New advertised-platform branch avoids this dependency entirely for OS lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: First OS resolution awaited full diagnostics and therefore this cold-token network dependency; no change to actual diagnostics operations requested for diagnostics themselves.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Old cold diagnostics delayed dialog formatting; new metadata branch removes the wait. Connectivity probes are not reached by this path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: First OS lookup per connection and token-context cache state, not number of selected files or environment rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Dialog's two lookups share one OS promise; diagnostics provider work is parallel but Copilot endpoint/login resolve the same context promise. No two-request fan-out is claimed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: OS lookups are shared/success-cached with a WeakMap and failure eviction. Endpoint/account lookup coalesces per token, with a 30-minute context and refresh buffer. Advertised root metadata is already present on normal native hosts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: scoped-dialog await, path-provider registration, old unconditional diagnostics call, existing advertised metadata and actual cold-context HTTP fetch are traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual cold-token network latency and cache warmth are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Concrete removed eager network dependency recorded as an internal regression-fix signal with base-line introducing-commit attribution; not a finding on this PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Withdraw registration, shut down the host, rotate credentials and recover from relay refusal/disconnection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Ingress and publication detach/close immediately on withdrawal or identity changes; optional offline check-in can remain pending without keeping ingress open. Recovery obtains fresh credentials/connects and reattaches retained mirroring; remote interactive readiness then depends on the response queue already analyzed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/missionControlEnvironment.ts: configure(undefined), recovery scheduling and _request; cloudSandboxAgentHostService.ts: reconnect/withdrawal
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send an offline heartbeat when permitted; refresh/reconnect relay credentials on recovery; stop recovery for permanently refused entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one applicable offline check-in per withdrawal; recovery attempts are scheduled/coalesced per generation with backoff up to 30 seconds and HTTP timeouts. Permanently refused native broker entries are unstaged so the outer remote service does not repeatedly redial cached credentials.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No native registration lifecycle/recovery traffic. The existing outer remote reconnect machinery is reused, and the new unstaging prevents its repeated redial on permanent refusal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Offline network completion is after ingress closure. Successful reconnect gates remote progress; unrelated local sessions are not waiting for cloud recovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retain bounded continuity spools across temporary withdrawal/reconnect and release them on owner/environment replacement/full disposal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Retention obeys mirror namespace session/frame/byte caps, not indefinite growth with every event. Reattachment reuses retained frames; disposal cancels scheduled publication and clears retained state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No native Mission Control continuity spool; existing local state lifetime is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Continuity bookkeeping is not awaited by local turns; replay delivery can contend with remote replies.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Lifecycle changes, transient reconnect attempts and retained admitted mirror data. Recovery is not multiplied by every stored session/environment row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Generation fencing/single in-flight work and scheduled retry/backoff prevent stale requests from replacing current configuration. Full disposal cancels metadata work/publication and tears down host-owned resources.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Temporary detach intentionally retains mirror/source continuity, while durable watermarks bound retention. Signing keys/credentials have explicit lifetimes; reconnect refreshes credentials. Permanent refusal removes staged entries rather than treating failure as a reusable successful credential cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: immediate close/detach, generation fencing, bounded spools, retry timers, permanent-entry withdrawal and disposal paths were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Disconnect prevalence and replay volume are unknown; retention budgets are statically established, not measured heap usage.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent high-confidence unbounded-retention/cleanup or retry-burst regression. Replay responsiveness is covered by the reported shared publisher finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass for PR #339513 against main base bd64649be19f2da0f09c2ab84c066c6c764b83be, head 680d699afd12266e3e42d5fb2db6b4723f77178b. Inspected the complete 87-file paginated inventory, all runtime diff pages and relevant test/documentation context; no binary/submodule review limitation. Submitted two concrete introduced regressions: global stop-and-wait relay publication and synchronous per-request filesystem authorization on the shared host event loop. Recorded one internally attributed fix for an unnecessary cold diagnostics/network dependency in OS resolution. Accounted for default-off startup, enablement/check-ins, discovery/attachment, streaming/replay, SDK metadata persistence, remote resources, path formatting and shutdown/recovery. Static read-only review: no execution/profiling; magnitudes are unmeasured, while reported mechanisms, effective cardinalities and critical-path placement are established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
